nodes.summary: Given a catalog $c$ and a list $L$ of catalogs, the result is $c$ itself if $L$ is empty, and otherwise the sorted merge of $c$ with the sample (every other element, starting with the first) of the first catalog of $L$.
nodes.title: Augmenting a catalog by the head of a list

nodes.summary: For catalogs $c$ and $a$, the augmentation of $c$ by $a$ is the sorted merge of $c$ with the sample of $a$ (every other element of $a$, starting with the first). In fractional cascading, $a$ is the next augmented catalog.
nodes.title: Augmenting a catalog by the next one

nodes.summary: For every catalog $c$, the list of augmented catalogs of the one-element list $[c]$ is $[c]$: the only augmented catalog is $c$ itself.
nodes.title: Augmenting a single catalog

nodes.summary: For a list of catalogs $c_1, \dots, c_k$, the augmented catalogs $A_1, \dots, A_k$ are built from the last one backwards: $A_k = c_k$, and for $i < k$, $A_i$ is the sorted merge of $c_i$ with the sample (every other element, starting with the first) of $A_{i+1}$. The empty list of catalogs has no augmented catalogs.
nodes.title: Augmented catalogs

nodes.summary: For every catalog $L$ and value $v$, the bridge pointer of $v$ into $L$ is at most the length of $L$.
nodes.title: Bridge pointers are at most the catalog length

nodes.summary: For a catalog $L$ and a value $v$, the bridge pointer of $v$ into $L$ is the number of elements of $L$ that are $\le v$.
nodes.title: Bridge pointer

nodes.summary: For catalogs $C$ and $L$, the bridge pointers of $C$ into $L$ form the list obtained by replacing each entry $v$ of $C$, in order, by the bridge pointer of $v$ into $L$.
nodes.title: Bridge pointer list

nodes.summary: For every value $x$ and every catalog $L$, the scan count of elements of $L$ that are $< x$ equals the lower bound of $x$ in $L$.
nodes.title: The scan count equals the lower bound

nodes.summary: For a value $x$ and a catalog $L$, the scan count of $x$ in $L$ is the number of elements of $L$ that are $< x$, computed by a direct scan: it is $0$ for the empty catalog, and for a catalog with head $a$ and tail $L'$ it is the scan count of $x$ in $L'$, plus $1$ if $a < x$.
nodes.title: Scan count of smaller elements

nodes.summary: For every value $x$, list of catalogs $C_0, \dots, C_{k-1}$ and index $i$: if $i < k$, the $i$-th position returned by searching all catalogs for $x$ is the lower bound of $x$ in $C_i$; if $i \ge k$, the search result has no $i$-th entry.
nodes.title: Search positions are lower bounds, index by index

nodes.summary: For lists $c$ and $d$ over a linearly ordered type, every entry $p$ of the list of bridge pointers of $c$ into $d$ satisfies $p \le |d|$, where $|d|$ is the length of $d$; so every recorded bridge pointer is a boundary index of $d$.
nodes.title: Bridge pointers are at most the next catalog's length

nodes.summary: For lists $c$ and $a$ over a linearly ordered type, the augmented catalog obtained by merging $c$ with the sample of $a$ has length at most $|c| + \lfloor (|a| + 1)/2 \rfloor$, the length of $c$ plus half the length of $a$ rounded up.
nodes.title: Length bound for one augmented catalog

nodes.summary: For lists $c$ and $a$ over a linearly ordered type, the augmented catalog obtained by merging $c$ with the sample $s(a)$ of $a$ has length $|c| + |s(a)|$.
nodes.title: Length of one augmented catalog

nodes.summary: For every list $cs$ of catalogs over a linearly ordered type, the list of augmented catalogs built from $cs$ has the same length as $cs$: there is one augmented catalog per catalog.
nodes.title: Number of augmented catalogs

nodes.summary: For lists $c$ and $d$ over a linearly ordered type, the list of bridge pointers of $c$ into $d$ has the same length as $c$: there is one bridge pointer per entry of $c$.
nodes.title: Number of bridge pointers

nodes.summary: For every list $cs = [c_1, \dots, c_k]$ of catalogs over a linearly ordered type, every augmented catalog built from $cs$ has length at most $|c_1| + \dots + |c_k|$.
nodes.title: Augmented catalogs are bounded by the total input size

nodes.summary: For every list $xs$ (over any type), the sample of $xs$, every other element starting with the first, has length at most the length of $xs$.
nodes.title: The sample is no longer than the list

nodes.summary: For every list $xs$ (over any type), the sample of $xs$ has length at most $\lfloor (|xs| + 1)/2 \rfloor$, half the length of $xs$ rounded up: for an even length $2m$ the bound is $m$, and for an odd length $2m + 1$ it is $m + 1$.
nodes.title: The sample has at most half the length, rounded up

nodes.summary: For every value $x$ and every list $cs$ of catalogs over a linearly ordered type, searching each catalog of $cs$ for $x$ gives a list of positions of the same length as $cs$.
nodes.title: One search position per catalog

nodes.summary: For every value $x$ and every list $cs$ of catalogs over a linearly ordered type, searching each augmented catalog built from $cs$ for $x$ gives a list of positions of the same length as $cs$.
nodes.title: One augmented search position per catalog

nodes.summary: For catalogs (finite lists) $L$ and $M$ over a linearly ordered type, the sorted merge of $L$ and $M$ has length equal to the length of $L$ plus the length of $M$.
nodes.title: Length of a sorted merge

nodes.summary: For a value $x$ and catalogs $c$ and $a$ over a linearly ordered type, the lower bound of $x$ in the augmented catalog of $c$ with $a$ (the sorted merge of $c$ with the sample of $a$) is at most the lower bound of $x$ in $c$ plus the lower bound of $x$ in $a$, where the lower bound of $x$ in a catalog is the number of its entries less than $x$.
nodes.title: Lower bound in an augmented catalog is at most the sum

nodes.summary: For a value $x$ and catalogs $c$ and $a$ over a linearly ordered type, the lower bound of $x$ in the augmented catalog of $c$ with $a$ (the sorted merge of $c$ with the sample of $a$) equals the lower bound of $x$ in $c$ plus the lower bound of $x$ in the sample of $a$, where the lower bound of $x$ in a catalog is the number of its entries less than $x$.
nodes.title: Lower bound in an augmented catalog splits

nodes.summary: For a value $x$ and a catalog $L$ over a linearly ordered type, the lower bound of $x$ in $L$ (the number of entries of $L$ less than $x$) is at most the length of $L$.
nodes.title: Lower bound is at most the catalog length

nodes.summary: For a value $x$ and a catalog $L$ over a linearly ordered type, the number of entries less than $x$ in the sample of $L$ (every other entry of $L$, starting with the first) is at most the number of entries of $L$ less than $x$.
nodes.title: Lower bound in a sample is at most the lower bound in the catalog

nodes.summary: For a value $x$ and catalogs $L$ and $M$ over a linearly ordered type, the lower bound of $x$ in the sorted merge of $L$ and $M$ equals the lower bound of $x$ in $L$ plus the lower bound of $x$ in $M$, where the lower bound of $x$ in a catalog is the number of its entries less than $x$.
nodes.title: Lower bound in a sorted merge splits

nodes.summary: For a value $x$ of a linearly ordered type and a catalog (finite list) $L$, the lower bound of $x$ in $L$ is the number of entries of $L$ that are less than $x$, counted with multiplicity. For a sorted catalog this is the first index whose entry is not less than $x$, or the length of $L$ if there is none.
nodes.title: Lower bound of a value in a catalog

nodes.summary: For catalogs $c$ and $a$ over a linearly ordered type, a value $v$ is an entry of the augmented catalog of $c$ with $a$ (the sorted merge of $c$ with the sample of $a$) if and only if $v$ is an entry of $c$ or an entry of the sample of $a$.
nodes.title: Membership in an augmented catalog

nodes.summary: For catalogs $c$ and $a$ over a linearly ordered type, every entry $v$ of the augmented catalog of $c$ with $a$ (the sorted merge of $c$ with the sample of $a$) is an entry of $c$ or an entry of $a$.
nodes.title: Entries of an augmented catalog come from the two catalogs

nodes.summary: For a catalog (finite list) $L$, every entry of the sample of $L$ (every other entry of $L$, starting with the first) is an entry of $L$.
nodes.title: Entries of a sample are entries of the catalog

nodes.summary: For lists $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ over a linear order and any element $v$, $v$ belongs to the sorted merge of $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ if and only if $v$ belongs to $\ell_1$ or to $\ell_2$.
nodes.title: Elements of a sorted merge

nodes.summary: For any lists $c$ and $a$ over a linear order, sorted or not, the augmented catalog obtained by merging $c$ with the sample of $a$ is sorted in nondecreasing order.
nodes.title: One augmentation step yields a sorted list

nodes.summary: If every catalog in a list of catalogs over a linear order is sorted in nondecreasing order, then every augmented catalog built from that list is sorted in nondecreasing order.
nodes.title: The augmented catalogs of sorted catalogs are sorted

nodes.summary: If a list over a linear order is sorted in nondecreasing order, then so is its sample.
nodes.title: The sample of a sorted list is sorted

nodes.summary: For any lists $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ over a linear order, sorted or not, their sorted merge is sorted in nondecreasing order.
nodes.title: A sorted merge is sorted

nodes.summary: For any lists $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ over a linear order, the sorted merge of $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ is a permutation of the concatenation of $\ell_1$ followed by $\ell_2$.
nodes.title: A sorted merge rearranges the concatenation

nodes.summary: For every flag $b$ (true or false) and every list $\ell$, the alternating selection of $\ell$ with initial flag $b$ is a sublist of $\ell$: it is obtained from $\ell$ by deleting some elements and keeping the rest in order.
nodes.title: Alternating selection gives a sublist

nodes.summary: For a flag $b$ (true or false) and a list $\ell$, the alternating selection of $\ell$ with initial flag $b$ is defined by recursion on $\ell$: the empty list gives the empty list; for a list with head $a$ and tail $\ell'$, if $b$ is true it keeps $a$ and continues on $\ell'$ with flag false, and if $b$ is false it drops $a$ and continues on $\ell'$ with flag true.
nodes.title: Alternating selection with a flag

nodes.summary: For every list $\ell$, the sample of $\ell$ is a sublist of $\ell$: it is obtained from $\ell$ by deleting some elements and keeping the rest in order.
nodes.title: The sample is a sublist

nodes.summary: The sample of a list $[x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots]$ is the list $[x_0, x_2, x_4, \dots]$ of every other element, starting with the first, in their original order.
nodes.title: Sample of a catalog

nodes.summary: For a value $x$, a catalog $c$ and a list of catalogs $cs$, searching $c$ followed by $cs$ for $x$ gives first the direct-scan count of the elements of $c$ that are $< x$, followed by the positions obtained by searching $cs$ for $x$.
nodes.title: Searching a nonempty list of catalogs

nodes.summary: For a value $x$ and a list of catalogs $c_1, \dots, c_k$, searching every catalog for $x$ returns the list whose $i$-th entry is the lower bound of $x$ in $c_i$, that is, the number of elements of $c_i$ that are $< x$.
nodes.title: Correctness of searching every catalog

nodes.summary: Let $x$ be a value and let $cs$ be a list of catalogs whose entry at index $i$ is the catalog $c$. Then searching every catalog of $cs$ for $x$ gives, at index $i$, the lower bound of $x$ in $c$ (the number of elements of $c$ that are $< x$), and this lower bound is at most the length of $c$.
nodes.title: Search positions are boundary indices

nodes.summary: Searching the empty list of catalogs for any value $x$ gives the empty list of positions.
nodes.title: Searching no catalogs

nodes.summary: For a value $x$ and a list of catalogs, the search returns, for each catalog in order, the number of its elements that are $< x$, computed by a direct scan of that catalog. This is the lower-bound position of $x$ in each catalog.
nodes.title: Searching every catalog

nodes.summary: For a value $x$ and a list of catalogs $cs$, searching every augmented catalog of $cs$ for $x$ returns, for each augmented catalog in order, the lower bound of $x$ in it, that is, the number of its elements that are $< x$.
nodes.title: Correctness of augmented search

nodes.summary: For a value $x$ and a list of catalogs, the augmented search builds the augmented catalogs and returns, for each augmented catalog in order, the number of its elements that are $< x$, computed by a direct scan of that catalog.
nodes.title: Searching every augmented catalog

nodes.summary: For lists $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2$ over a linearly ordered type, their sorted merge is the result of merge sort, with respect to $\le$, applied to the concatenation of $\ell_1$ followed by $\ell_2$.
nodes.title: Sorted merge of two catalogs

nodes.summary: For every catalog $L$, twice the length of the sample of $L$ is at most the length of $L$ plus one.
nodes.title: Doubled sample length bound

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
